articles.summary: Surf Air Mobility (NYSE: SRFM) (“Surf Air Mobility” or the “Company”), a leading air mobility platform, announced today that Company executives attended the launch meeting for Project Nexus on Thursday, September 10, at Alliance Field in Fort Worth, Texas (AFW). Project Nexus is the Federal Aviation Administration's eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) initiative awarded to North Texas, bringing together a coalition of the industry's leading eVTOL manufacturers, including BETA Technologies (“BETA”), Joby Aviation, and Archer Aviation. The program is designed to establish the operational, regulatory, and infrastructure framework needed to integrate electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft into the national airspace. Surf Air Mobility's attendance reinforces its position as the platform that eVTOL and Advanced Air Mobility manufacturers will rely on to bring next-generation aircraft into commercial service. articles.title: Surf Air Mobility Attends FAA's Project Nexus eIPP Event, Reinforcing Its Position as the Commercial Platform for Advanced Air Mobility

Mokulele’s Hawai ʻ i operations support Surf Air Mobility ’ s broader platform, SurfOS software, and Advanced Air Mobility strategy, and positions Hawai ʻ i as a showcase for electric flight. Surf Air Mobility Inc. (NYSE: SRFM) (“Surf Air Mobility” or the “Company”) today announced that its airline subsidiary, Mokulele Airlines (“Mokulele”), has been awarded a new Essential Air Service (“EAS”) contract by the U.S. Department of Transportation (“DOT”) to continue scheduled air service to Lanaʻi, Hawaiʻi. The contract represents $19.4 million in EAS subsidies, excluding incremental passenger fare revenue, over four years, doubling the term of the prior contract, and provides contracted revenue through August 2030.
